examples: Her willingness to help made the project smooth.
Her willingness to mentor junior staff impressed the board.
The team's willingness to change made the migration succeed.

example: Please wipe the table before the client arrives.
usage: Use to clean or dry a surface by rubbing it, or to remove data.
story: He wiped the tears from his eyes.
examples: Please wipe the table before the client arrives.
Wipe the screen gently with a soft cloth.
The technician wiped the old files from the server.

example: Her wit made the long meeting more enjoyable.
usage: Use for quick, clever humour or a sharp intelligence.
story: He answered the tough question with great wit.
examples: Her wit made the long meeting more enjoyable.
The speaker used wit to keep the audience engaged.
Use your wit to find a creative solution.

example: The withdrawal of the offer surprised the team.
intent: Describing removal of support or money
usage: Use when something is taken back or money is taken out.
story: The bank processed the cash withdrawal quickly.
examples: The withdrawal of the offer surprised the team.
The withdrawal of the funding delayed the expansion plan.
Withdrawal from the joint venture was announced on Monday.

example: The team had a workout of the new software features.
usage: Use when you go through a task to test or practice it.
story: We ran a quick workout before the presentation.
examples: The team had a workout of the new software features.
The team ran a workout to test the new dashboard.
A quick workout of the approval steps found a bottleneck.

example: The delay could worsen if we do not act now.
usage: Use when a situation becomes more serious or difficult.
story: Cash flow began to worsen in the summer.
examples: The delay could worsen if we do not act now.
Delays could worsen if the approvals remain pending.
The currency crisis may worsen our import costs next quarter.

example: Employees may leave early to attend worship on Friday.
usage: Use for religious devotion or to admire someone greatly.
story: The village gathered for worship at the old temple.
examples: Employees may leave early to attend worship on Friday.
The church holds worship services every Sunday.
Fans worship the singer and attend every concert.

example: The training was worthwhile for the entire sales team.
usage: Use when something is useful enough to be worth the effort.
story: The project proved worthwhile after the first quarter.
examples: The training was worthwhile for the entire sales team.
The new software proved worthwhile after only one quarter.
Attending the procurement seminar was worthwhile for our buyers.

example: The project is worthy of the board's full support.
usage: Use to mean deserving of respect or attention.
story: She was a worthy winner of the award.
examples: The project is worthy of the board's full support.
Every good idea is worthy of consideration.
The charity is a worthy cause for our donations.

example: Please do not yell across the office floor.
usage: Use to shout loudly, often in anger or excitement.
story: The coach began to yell instructions from the sideline.
examples: Please do not yell across the office floor.
He yelled for help when the machine caught fire.
Fans yelled with joy when the team scored.

example: The investment yield was high this year.
usage: Use for the output or return from something.
story: The farm's yield improved after the new irrigation.
examples: The investment yield was high this year.
The investment yield exceeded expectations for the third year.
Improved processes raised the production yield significantly.

example: The youngster joined the team as an intern.
usage: Use when speaking informally about a young person.
story: The youngster learned fast and got a full-time offer.
examples: The youngster joined the team as an intern.
The youngster completed the sales course with top marks.
A youngster from our internship program joined the team.
